description: DCS World Air Defense Threat Database with AGM-88 HARM Targeting Data

strategic_sams.name: SA-2 Guideline
strategic_sams.vulnerabilities: Distinctive radar signature, susceptible to SEAD, slow deployment
strategic_sams.notes: Long-range strategic SAM. Fan Song radar very distinctive on RWR. Vulnerable target for HARM. Slow to relocate.

strategic_sams.name: SA-3 Goa
strategic_sams.vulnerabilities: Medium-range engagement capability, vulnerable to SEAD
strategic_sams.notes: Mobile SAM system. Low Blow radar less distinctive than Fan Song. Moderate altitude capability. Good medium-range threat.

strategic_sams.name: SA-5 Gammon
strategic_sams.vulnerabilities: Very long engagement envelope, slow reload, fixed site
strategic_sams.countermeasures: Low-level penetration, maneuver, jamming, high-speed evasion
strategic_sams.notes: Extremely long-range SAM. High minimum altitude. Slow to reload and relocate. Significant strategic threat.

strategic_sams.name: SA-10 Grumble
strategic_sams.vulnerabilities: Can be jammed, vulnerable to SEAD, ARH missiles susceptible to chaff
strategic_sams.countermeasures: Chaff corridors, ECM, maneuver, terrain masking, ARM attacks
strategic_sams.notes: Modern integrated SAM system. Mobile or semi-mobile. Excellent long-range capability. Significant threat to all altitudes.

strategic_sams.name: SA-11 Gadfly
strategic_sams.vulnerabilities: Mobile but slower than TOR, vulnerable to SEAD, ARH missiles
strategic_sams.countermeasures: Chaff, ECM, maneuver, low-level flight, ARM targeting
strategic_sams.notes: Highly mobile integrated SAM system. Good all-altitude capability. Straight Flush radar is distinctive HARM target.

strategic_sams.name: SA-6 Gainful
strategic_sams.vulnerabilities: Mobile system, susceptible to SEAD, ARH design vulnerable to chaff
strategic_sams.countermeasures: Chaff, maneuver, low-level penetration, ARM tactics
strategic_sams.notes: Mobile SAM with distinctive Straight Flush radar. Primary threat in medium range. Good horizontal coverage.

medium_range_sams.name: SA-8 Gecko
medium_range_sams.vulnerabilities: Limited range, IR-only missiles, can be outrun by fast jets
medium_range_sams.notes: IR-guided missiles only. Limited range but highly mobile. Visible threat in low-altitude environment.

medium_range_sams.name: SA-15 Gauntlet
medium_range_sams.vulnerabilities: Limited range, self-contained system, vulnerable to stand-off missiles
medium_range_sams.countermeasures: Stand-off employment, chaff, maneuver, speed advantage
medium_range_sams.notes: Modern short-range SAM. Highly mobile. Good against cruise missiles and low-level aircraft. Eight missile capacity.

medium_range_sams.name: SA-19 Grison
medium_range_sams.track_radar: Integrated radar for both missiles and guns
medium_range_sams.vulnerabilities: Limited range, dual-system complexity, vulnerable to stand-off weapons
medium_range_sams.notes: Integrated SAM/AAA system. Eight missiles plus dual 30mm guns. Highly mobile. Effective against rotary-wing and low-level threats.

medium_range_sams.name: Roland
medium_range_sams.vulnerabilities: Limited range, command-guided variant slower reaction, vulnerable to jamming
medium_range_sams.notes: Western short-range SAM. Mobile system. Radar and IR variants. Good against cruise missiles.

short_range_shorad.name: SA-9 Gaskin
short_range_shorad.vulnerabilities: IR-only, very short range, vulnerable to flares and speed advantage
short_range_shorad.notes: Portable IR SAM. Very limited range and altitude. Threat mainly to slow-moving or hovering aircraft.

short_range_shorad.name: SA-13 Gopher
short_range_shorad.vulnerabilities: Primarily IR, limited range, vulnerable to flares and stand-off tactics
short_range_shorad.notes: Self-propelled SHORAD system. Improved Strela variant. Semi-automatic tracking. IR primary guidance.

short_range_shorad.name: SA-18 Igla
short_range_shorad.vulnerabilities: Portable, single-shot, IR-only, very short range, easily evaded by maneuver
short_range_shorad.notes: Man-portable IR SAM. Single operator. Very short range. Threat primarily to slow-moving or hovering platforms.

aaa_systems.name: ZSU-23-4 Shilka
aaa_systems.vulnerabilities: Limited range, radar can be jammed, vulnerable to stand-off fire
aaa_systems.countermeasures: Stand-off employment, jamming, maneuver, speed advantage
aaa_systems.notes: Tracked self-propelled AAA. Gun Dish radar distinctive signature. Effective against low-level aircraft. Primary anti-aircraft gun of Soviet forces.

aaa_systems.name: ZU-23-2
aaa_systems.vulnerabilities: No radar, towed (slow displacement), limited range, vulnerable to stand-off tactics
aaa_systems.notes: Towed twin 23mm gun. No radar guidance. Effective against low-level threats. Limited engagement range.

aaa_systems.name: Gepard
aaa_systems.vulnerabilities: Radar can be jammed, vulnerable to stand-off missiles
aaa_systems.notes: Modern tracked self-propelled AAA. Dual 35mm guns. Good mid-altitude capability. Western air defense gun.

aaa_systems.name: Vulcan M163
aaa_systems.vulnerabilities: High rate of fire creates tracking challenges, vulnerable to stand-off fire
aaa_systems.notes: Tracked self-propelled AAA. 20mm Vulcan rotary cannon. Excellent rate of fire. Primary US air defense gun.

aaa_systems.name: Bofors 40mm
aaa_systems.vulnerabilities: Limited range, often optical guidance, vulnerable to stand-off fire
aaa_systems.notes: Classic 40mm gun. Widely deployed. L/70 variant has better ballistics. Often used without radar.

ewr_systems.name: 1L13 EWR
ewr_systems.vulnerabilities: Fixed site, vulnerable to cruise missiles, large radar signature
ewr_systems.countermeasures: High-altitude maneuver, stand-off ARM attacks, jamming
ewr_systems.notes: VHF surveillance radar. Large coverage area. Fixed or semi-mobile deployment. Excellent long-range coverage.

ewr_systems.name: Flat Face
ewr_systems.vulnerabilities: Mobile site, distinctive radar signature, vulnerable to SEAD
ewr_systems.countermeasures: ECM, maneuver, low-level flight, ARM tactics
ewr_systems.notes: Mobile surveillance radar. Used as search radar for SA-6, SA-11 systems. Distinctive HARM target when used with Straight Flush.

ewr_systems.name: Dog Ear
ewr_systems.vulnerabilities: Towed, distinctive antenna signature, vulnerable to stand-off attacks
ewr_systems.notes: VHF surveillance radar. Mobile/towed variant of early warning system. Good long-range coverage.

ewr_systems.name: Hawk SR
ewr_systems.vulnerabilities: Semi-mobile, vulnerable to SEAD when active, radar can be jammed
ewr_systems.countermeasures: ECM, stand-off ARM employment, high-altitude maneuver, jamming
ewr_systems.notes: Pulse-Doppler 3D radar. Part of integrated Hawk air defense system. Good all-altitude coverage.

ewr_systems.name: Patriot STR
ewr_systems.vulnerabilities: Phased array can be jammed, vulnerable to SEAD when active
ewr_systems.countermeasures: ECM, stand-off ARM employment, jamming, maneuver
ewr_systems.notes: Modern phased array radar. Integrated search and track. Excellent all-altitude capability. Primary NATO air defense radar.

western_sams.name: Hawk
western_sams.vulnerabilities: SARH missiles vulnerable to chaff, can be jammed, susceptible to ARM attacks
western_sams.countermeasures: Chaff corridors, ECM, maneuver, ARM tactics, low-level penetration
western_sams.notes: Integrated air defense system. Semi-mobile platform. Good mid-altitude coverage. Extensively deployed NATO SAM.

western_sams.name: Patriot
western_sams.guidance_type: Semi-active radar homing (SARH) / Active radar homing (ARH-PAC3)
western_sams.vulnerabilities: PAC-2 SARH vulnerable to chaff, both variants vulnerable to ARMs, can be jammed
western_sams.countermeasures: Chaff corridors, ECM, maneuver, ARM tactics, speed advantage for long-range evasion
western_sams.notes: Modern integrated air defense system. Mobile platform. Excellent long-range all-altitude capability. Primary NATO long-range SAM.

western_sams.name: NASAMS
western_sams.vulnerabilities: ARH missiles with typical AMRAAM vulnerabilities, can be jammed, susceptible to ECM
western_sams.countermeasures: Chaff, ECM, maneuver, terrain masking, AMRAAM-specific evasion tactics
western_sams.notes: Modern network-centric air defense. Uses AMRAAM missiles. Highly mobile. Excellent integration potential with other systems.

western_sams.name: Rapier
western_sams.vulnerabilities: Limited range, optical guidance can be affected by weather, vulnerable to stand-off employment
western_sams.countermeasures: Stand-off employment, maneuver, weather exploitation, flares (IR variant)
western_sams.notes: British self-propelled SAM. Command guidance or IR homing variants. Good close-in air defense capability.

table_1.name: SAM Systems
table_1.description: Strategic and tactical surface-to-air missile systems
table_1.frequency: Primary threat to fixed-wing aircraft at altitude

table_2.name: EWR/Radar Systems
table_2.description: Early warning radars and surveillance systems
table_2.frequency: Primary threat for SEAD operations targeting radar sources

table_3.name: AAA and Other
table_3.description: Anti-aircraft artillery and integrated short-range systems
table_3.frequency: Primary threat at low altitudes and to rotary-wing aircraft

HI.criteria: Long-range SAMs with integrated search/track radars. Poses significant threat across wide altitude envelope.

MED.criteria: Medium-range systems with moderate threat envelope. Mobile systems with good coverage.

LO.criteria: Short-range systems with limited threat envelope. Primarily defensive systems.

general: Chaff deployment in corridors for SARH missiles
Terrain masking and low-level flight below radar coverage
High-altitude maneuver for systems with altitude limitations
Formation flying for mutual support and deception
sead_operations: Stand-off ARM employment (AGM-88 HARM) against radar emitters
Wild Weasel tactics with dedicated SEAD support
Suppression of radar through dedicated fighter cover
Rotating strike packages to prevent radar reset
Use of expendable platforms to draw fire
GPS-guided munitions against known radar locations
low_altitude: Concentrated chaff dispensing in threat zones
Quick egress and altitude changes to defeat tracking
Cross-pop maneuvers to break missile locks

VHF.characteristics: Long-range, poor low-altitude coverage, difficult to jam

E-F band.characteristics: Medium range, good tracking, moderate jamming resistance

G-band.characteristics: Medium range, distinctive RWR signature, vulnerable to SEAD

X-band.characteristics: Short-range, good resolution, easily jammed, weather susceptible

C-band.characteristics: All-weather, good range, phased array capability, jamming resistant

deployment_notes.strategic: Long-range SAMs protecting key targets. Typically semi-fixed with limited mobility.
deployment_notes.operational: Systems providing air defense for operational areas. Mobile with good reaction time.
deployment_notes.tactical: Short-range systems providing low-altitude protection. Highly mobile platforms.
deployment_notes.regimental: Integrated defense for regiment-sized units. Multiple platform types.
deployment_notes.divisional: Air defense integrated with division. Multiple layers of defense.
deployment_notes.corps_army: Strategic-level air defense. Phased array and integrated systems.

notes.harm_employment: AGM-88 HARM targeting codes listed correspond to official USAF HARM Tables of Emitters. Actual in-game implementation may vary based on DCS World version.
notes.system_accuracy: Technical specifications reflect DCS World in-game values as of 2026-04-10. Real-world systems may differ significantly.
notes.tactical_guidance: Evasion tactics and threat assessment are generic guidelines. Actual air defense suppression should account for specific mission parameters and environmental factors.
notes.western_harm_codes: Western air defense systems (Patriot, Hawk, etc.) are not assigned specific HARM codes in standard targeting tables, as they are typically friendly forces.
notes.mobile_vs_fixed: Mobile systems can displace after detection. Fixed sites require longer to relocate. Reload times reflect in-game mechanics.
